 BEND, Ore. -- A 4.3 magnitude earthquake in northeastern Oregon near the Idaho border Monday night became the strongest quake recorded in eastern Oregon in more than 30 years, according to local reports.
 More than 100 people reported feeling the shaking after the earthquake struck just before midnight about 12 miles outside Joseph, though no damage was reported.
 The Pacific Northwest Seismic Network told a local newspaper the earthquake struck along an unmapped section of the Wallowa Fault.
